payload.statement: Mission update received 2026-07-12: the Laboratory Protocol is frozen at five obligations — Identity, Grounding, Provenance, Explicit Judgment, Sealing. Continuity was eliminated as derivable. The burden of proof reversed: implementation must justify architectural change. Full text preserved at laboratory/PROTOCOL.md and cabinet CAB-008.

provenance.intention: preserve the mandate as an observation in the record itself

payload.statement: The five obligations arrived as names; the Record contains no authoritative definitions beyond them. Engineering interpretations were adopted and written to laboratory/PROTOCOL.md.

payload.conclusion: The engineering interpretations in laboratory/PROTOCOL.md are adopted as implementation law for this Laboratory until challenged or until authoritative definitions arrive.
payload.reasoning: The mandate grants engineering authority and forbids stopping for engineering uncertainty; the obligations map cleanly onto existing corpus primitives (P-002, P-006, P-008, P-009/010/011, P-013), so interpretation implements existing principles rather than inventing new ones (stop condition 3 not triggered). Recording the interpretations as a challengeable artifact keeps them revisable.

provenance.intention: make the adoption of interpretations an explicit judgment, not a side effect

payload.question: Do the five obligations have authoritative definitions beyond their names? The interpretations in laboratory/PROTOCOL.md are provisional until the Reality seat confirms or corrects them.

payload.summary: First session: mandate preserved, protocol interpretations adopted by explicit judgment, definitional gap recorded as an open unknown, the Laboratory given identity in its own record. Kernel extended to protocol conformance (16 tests green). The record is now continuable by any Participant from this file alone.

provenance.intention: depart and hand the Laboratory to whoever arrives next

payload.statement: The Laboratory grew for daily use: a write-capable CLI (arrive/observe/entity/assert/judge/unknown/resolve/evidence/seal + explain/sessions), a tip guard refusing forked history when Participants overlap, sessions derived from seals, and a web room (laboratory/record/index.html) that re-verifies the chain in the reader's browser. 18 tests green.

provenance.intention: record the growth milestone as an observation in the record it improved

payload.conclusion: Arrival no longer requires writing code; the record is discoverable from shell and browser; concurrent Participants cannot corrupt the chain.
payload.reasoning: Each improvement was chosen by the mandate's question — does this make the Laboratory better for the next Participant. The CLI removes the largest arrival barrier; the tip guard turns a silent corruption into an explicit recoverable refusal; the web room makes verification public without tooling. No new protocol concepts were needed: sessions are pure derivation over seals.

provenance.intention: state the engineering judgment explicitly rather than leaving it implicit in commits

payload.conclusion: The judgment above rests on the milestone observation.
